Clothing & Textile Restoration

Water & Flood Damage Clothing and Textile Restoration in Pennsylvania

Leaks, flooding and firefighting water can affect clothing, bedding and household textiles. Prompt attention matters, but the source of water and the material involved determine what may be safely considered for restoration.

What makes water damage different?

Water can cause dye transfer, shrinkage, staining, odor and changes to fabric texture. Moisture trapped in folded or stored textiles can lead to additional damage. Water from a clean supply line differs from sewage or floodwater, which may contain hazardous contaminants.

Which belongings may be assessed?

Depending on condition and exposure, affected garments, linens, bedding, drapery and certain specialty textiles may be considered. Items exposed to sewage, floodwater or other hazardous contamination may be unsafe to recover; professional safety advice takes priority.

What to do after water exposure

Do not mix wet and unaffected garments. Avoid sealing wet textiles in closed bags for extended periods. Follow property safety instructions, and do not handle items exposed to potentially contaminated water without appropriate guidance.

How ACR approaches the next step

Contact American Clothing Restoration with the type and source of water damage, approximate time since exposure, and the textiles involved. Each item must be evaluated individually; neither cleaning nor full recovery is guaranteed.

The next step

Ask about your affected clothing and textiles.
